event.summary: Removed account selection does not turn legacy container launch into host execution
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: Considered whether deleting the legacy account-selection and checkout-root authority helpers could cause an old container launch to execute against the outside host or expose a broader host checkout. Such a route would be security-impacting (could-be-highest: true). Source refutation: the replacement container.rs:1-5 and :79-95 has only removal coordinates, with no creation or exec implementation. launch.rs:1169-1175 explicitly rejects a retained LaunchSpec carrying container before checkout preparation or execution, rather than dropping the field. service/core.rs:3729-3738 provides the retired-launch guard. The assigned working_copies.rs deletion removes the specialized managed_checkout_root selector; the ordinary identity-checked cwd_is_managed implementation remains at :1202-1224. A pinned supervisor-source search finds no remaining managed_checkout_root, choose_account, initialize_account or HostAccount callers. Contract: SPEC.md, Retired containerized sessions, :4816-4824 states 'The old launcher switch and account-selection flow are gone.' SPEC_impl.md, Rootless Podman sessions, :8647-8656 requires refusing all other lifecycle/terminal/exec paths and removing account selection once no creation/open path remains. Suggested bucket if the suspected route existed: highest; current conclusion is source-refuted, confidence confirmed for the removed account helper and launch-shim route. proposed_drop: source refutation by explicit retained-spec refusal and removal-only runtime, not merely acceptance by spec. possible_cover: none. Caveats: no execution performed; the separate lifecycle/file-path groups own a full audit of every retirement guard. This candidate preserves the potential outside-host execution/broadened file-authority consequence; it does not claim all retirement interfaces were reviewed here.

event.summary: Per-launch uncertainty still protects surviving checkout claims
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether the new per-launch uncertainty wording masks cleanup deleting a claim still being used to prepare a checkout after supervisor restart. The original suspected consequence was recursive removal of a launch's claimed tree while it was in use (could-be-highest: true for loss of user-owned work if such a route existed). Source refutation: the assigned patch changes only comments. LiveClaims::protects at spare_checkouts.rs:45-50 retains the global uncertain flag OR the exact (session,generation) pair, and sweep_namespace at :542-549 skips protected claimed names before discard_child. The startup caller service/core.rs:7822-7896 derives exact-generation protection from terminal-host evidence, treating unattributed observations, missing/unreadable provenance, and missing/unreadable preparation state conservatively; NotStarted and CloneStarted are both protected. repo_cache.rs:120-123 skips a held cache flock before any trash or spare cleanup, matching its changed terminal-host comment at :84-91. Contract: SPEC_impl.md, Owned checkout admission and lifetime, :3966-3974 states 'failed or uncertain liveness observations retain possible claims rather than inferring abandonment.' Suggested bucket if the suspected destruction route existed: highest; current confidence confirmed source-refuted for the changed comments and their direct consumers. proposed_drop: code preserves both global and exact-generation claim protection and no behavior is changed by either assigned comment patch. possible_cover: none. Caveats: source-only; no execution observed, and this does not independently certify all terminal-host liveness implementation owned by adjacent groups.

At 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 core.rs:7837-7866 skips protection for a row with no in-memory terminal and stored TerminalKind::Tmux, without observing migration success. old_terminals.rs:306-318 logs failed reap, and :351-356 proceeds after its deadline. spare_take.rs:38-40 takes no cache lock; :156-181 moves children by the retained claim-directory handle into the allocated directory, then unlinks the old claim name, so parking the claim cannot exclude those child moves. spare_checkouts.rs:542-556 selects an unprotected claim and :611-618 parks then opens/removes it. checkout_trash.rs:320-349 retains opened child directory handles and traverses them; :351-353 deletes files through those handles. The origin itself fails on unlink of the parked claim (:176-181), so this is not a claim that its own later merge/hook/agent writes lost work. Current TLDR: a failed attempt to end an old checkout preparation can let startup delete work in that checkout even while a separate retained session uses it. Current suggested bucket: highest, for the established conditional source route to loss of borrower-owned work.
